turns.content: Yeah, I'm beat. Ten hours hauling spiral duct in this heat and my shoulders are fried. Group chat's blowing up with Lake Chelan photos—Toby, Julian, Sam all there. Nobody said a word to me about it. And now Mateo needs my answer on Friday duckpin bowling by Wednesday or I eat the forfeit fee. Just feels like I'm the only one still doing real work while they're all remote and planning trips without me.

Ugh, ten hours of hauling spiral duct in this heat? That's brutal — your shoulders have every right to be done. Take the win of surviving that, at least.

And the Chelan thing stings, and I don't want to gloss over it. Finding out through group chat photos instead of an actual invite is a specific kind of lousy feeling — like you're watching your own friendship happen without you in it. It's fair to feel that. It might not even be deliberate exclusion (people get lazy about inviting, especially when they assume you're working), but the impact on you is real either way. If it's bugging you this much, it might be worth a low-key text to one of them — "looked like fun, would've come" — just to put it on the radar without making it a whole thing.

On the bowling: that one's actually in your control, which is nice when everything else feels like it isn't. Do you *want* to go Friday? If yes, just message Mateo now and knock it off your plate — one less thing rattling around. If your body's wrecked and you'd rather crash, that's a legit answer too, just tell him before Wednesday so you're not out the forfeit fee.

So: ice those shoulders, hydrate, and decide the bowling thing tonight so it's not looming. Which way are you leaning on Friday?
I don't know about texting Toby. That feels like asking to be included after the fact, which is worse than not being included at all. They had two weeks to say something. Silence says enough.

Yeah, I get that — reaching out after the fact can feel like you're auditioning for a spot they didn't offer, and that's a worse feeling than the exclusion itself. That's a totally legitimate read, and you don't have to do it.

The only thing I'd gently put out there: silence is real, but it's also ambiguous. Sometimes it means "we didn't think of him," which is careless but not malicious — especially if they know you're grinding long hours and just assumed you couldn't come. Doesn't make it hurt less, but it might not mean what it feels like it means at 10pm after a rough shift.

But here's the thing — you don't have to figure that out tonight. You're exhausted and everything's going to read worse right now. The Chelan photos will still be there Thursday, and your feelings about them will be a lot clearer once you've slept and your shoulders aren't screaming.

The one thing with a deadline is Mateo. That's worth deciding while your brain still has a few watts left. Gut check: if you weren't tired and annoyed at the world, would Friday duckpin sound fun or like a chore?

Yeah. I hear you. I'm just... not there yet on texting them.

The bowling thing though—I want to go. I just don't know if I'll have the gas left by Friday.

Totally fair — park the friend thing for now. No rule says you have to resolve it this week.

On bowling: since you *want* to go, tell Mateo yes now. That locks it in before Wednesday and gets it off your mental plate. Wanting to go is actually the hard part — energy is the fixable part.

A few things that might help you have gas by Friday:

- **Protect Thursday night.** That's your recovery window. Early dinner, early bed, no staying up doomscrolling the Chelan photos (seriously — that'll drain you more than the duct work did).
- **Tell Mateo your situation.** Something like "I'm in, but I'm coming off a brutal week, so I might be running on fumes." That way if you show up wrecked, nobody's surprised, and it's low-stakes. Showing up tired to bowl badly with friends is still a good night — duckpin is basically designed for that.
- **Give yourself an out that isn't a forfeit.** If Friday morning you're genuinely dead, you can still message Mateo before the day's gone — bailing day-of to a friend who knows the context is way different than ghosting and eating the fee.

So: text Mateo tonight while you're thinking about it. One sentence, done. Then ice the shoulders and go to bed. Deal?

Yeah, I'll text Mateo tonight. That part's straightforward.

The Chelan thing though—I just checked the chat to see if maybe I missed something. And I did. Toby sent a poll two weeks ago asking who was free. I never saw it. It was buried under a dozen muted notifications from my apprenticeship study group. I was sitting my union exams that week.

Oh. Okay, that reframes things pretty significantly.

So it wasn't "they didn't want you" — it was a poll buried under study group notifications during the exact week you were sitting union exams. That's not exclusion, that's a group chat being a terrible communication tool. The silence you read as a message was actually just... chaos and bad timing.

Which, weirdly, can be its own kind of frustrating — you spent a whole evening feeling like the odd man out, and it turns out nobody dropped the ball on purpose. The hurt was real, but the story behind it was wrong.

I'm not saying you have to text Toby tonight or anything. But when you're ready, this actually makes reaching out way easier — because now it's not "can I come next time," it's just "just saw the poll, it got buried under my exam stuff, looked like a great trip." That's not asking to be included. That's just closing the loop on a misfire. Way less ego on the line.

And for what it's worth — you weren't sitting out while they planned without you. You were passing your union exams. That's not nothing. That's the opposite of nothing.

Text Mateo, get some sleep, and maybe mute the study group chat for a bit so actual plans don't get buried again.
Yeah. I see it now. Poll was up for three days. I was in the exam room for most of it, and the rest I was too fried to scroll past the study chat.

That tracks. Exam weeks are a total blackout — you're either in the room or in recovery mode, and everything outside that bubble basically doesn't exist. Three days is nothing when you're in that state. Nobody's fault, just bad timing stacked on bad timing.

So the whole "silence says enough" thing — turns out the silence was saying "he's busy, we'll catch him next time," and your phone was saying nothing at all because it was muted under 47 messages about conduit bending or whatever the study group was going off about.

You're in a good spot now, honestly: Mateo gets his yes tonight, the Chelan thing turns out to be a logistics glitch instead of a friendship wound, and you've got a legit reason to text Toby whenever you feel like it — no groveling required.

Last item on the agenda: shoulders, ice, bed. You've earned all three.
